DECISION 
I. 
INTRODUCTION 
A. 
SUMMARY 
The Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (Authority or PURA) directs Brass City 
Community Television, Inc. (Brass City) to assume the Community Access Provider 
designation as well as the responsibilities for and the control of operations at the access 
facility, which are currently designated to and controlled by Skye Cable XII, Inc. (Skye). 
B. 
CONDUCT OF THE PROCEEDING 
On January 11, 2024, Skye filed an inquiry with the Authority as to the procedure 
to transfer its Community Access Provider designation as well as responsibility for and 
control of operations of the access facility (Inquiry). On March 4, 2024, the Authority 
issued a Notice of Proceeding and Procedural Order (NOP) directing Skye to file an 
accounting of its assets addressing the process for nonprofits to request to assume 
responsibility. The Authority requested that any community-based nonprofit organization 
that desired to assume responsibility for the Company’s community access operations 
file a petition with the Authority in accordance with General Statutes § 16-331a(c) not later 
than April 8, 2024. NOP. 
On March 19, 2024, Skye filed an accounting of its assets. Skye Corresp., Mar. 19, 
2024. The Authority received a petition to assume responsibility for Skye’s community 
access provider operations from Brass City on April 8, 2024. Brass City Corresp., Apr. 4, 
2024 (Petition). 
The Authority offered parties and intervenors the opportunity for a hearing with a 
date certain to request the hearing. Notice of Hearing, May 29, 2024. No parties or 
intervenors requested a hearing. As a result, the hearing was canceled. Notice of 
Cancelation of Hearing, June 7, 2024. On July 11, 2024, the Authority issued a proposed 
final decision and offered the parties and intervenors the chance to provide written 
exceptions. The Authority received no written exceptions. 
C. 
PARTIES AND INTERVENORS 
The Authority recognized the following as parties to this proceeding: Alphonso L 
Coles, Brass City Community Television, Inc., 140 Fulkerson Drive, #3E, Waterbury, CT 
06708; Stephen W. Mindera, Jr., Skye Cable XIII, Inc., 117 Sharon Road, Waterbury, CT 
06705; Office of Education, Outreach, and Enforcement, Ten Franklin Square, New 
Britain, CT 06051; Office of Consumer Counsel (OCC), Ten Franklin Square, New Britain, 
CT 06051; and the Commissioner of the Department of Energy and Environmental 
Protection (DEEP), 79 Elm Street, Hartford, CT 06106. 
II. 
STANDARD OF REVIEW 
General Statutes § 16-331a (l) provides that when “an organization assigned 
responsibility for community access operations which organization ceases to provide 
such operations” it “shall transfer its assets to the successor organization assigned such 

Docket No. 24-01-41 
Page 2 

responsibility or, if no successor organization is assigned such responsibility, to another 
nonprofit organization within the franchise area selected by the authority.” 
General Statutes § 16-331a(c) addresses the type of information the Authority 
must assess when a nonprofit seeks to take over community access operations from a 
multichannel video programming distributor (MVPD). The criteria for selection provides 
guidance to the Authority in this proceeding. The Authority reviews the following criteria 
in this docket: 
(1) The recommendations of the advisory council and of the municipalities 
in the franchise area; 
(2) a review of the organization's or the company's performance in providing 
community access programming; 
(3) the operating plan submitted by the organization and the company for 
providing community access programming; 
(4) the experience in community access programming of the organization; 
(5) the organization's and the company's proposed budget, including 
expenses for salaries, consultants, attorneys, and other professionals; 
(6) the quality and quantity of the programming to be created, promoted or 
facilitated by the organization or the company; 
(7) a review of the organization's procedures to ensure compliance with 
federal and state law, including the regulations of Connecticut state 
agencies; and 
(8) any other criteria determined to be relevant by the authority. 

General Statutes § 16-331a(c). “If the authority selects an organization to provide 
community access operations, the [MVPD] shall provide financial and technical support 
to the organization in an amount to be determined by the authority.” Id. 
III. 
AUTHORITY ANALYSIS 
A. 
BRASS CITY APPLICATION 
Brass City is a community-based nonprofit entity, headquartered in Waterbury, 
which was established and registered with the Secretary of the State in February 2024 
and is spearheaded by Alphonso Coles, Brass City’s Executive Director. Petition, p. 1. 
Colleen Fitzpatrick serves as Brass City’s Program Director. Id. Brass City’s Petition sets 
forth the qualifications of Mr. Coles and Ms. Fitzpatrick, Brass City’s plan for operation, 
and its proposed community operations. The Authority addresses the eight guiding 
statutory criteria below. 
1. The recommendations of the advisory council and of the municipalities 
in the franchise area. 
Brass City’s Petition included a letter from the Greater Waterbury Cable Council 
(GWCC). Petition, Att. 4.1. GWCC endorsed Mr. Coles’ proposal to take over community 
access operations stating that “Al Coles is not only well-acquainted with the current 
operations at SKYE but also brings with him a network of quality professionals who have 
previously enriched SKYE with their administrative and instructional expertise.” Id.

Page 3 

GCWW acknowledged Mr. Coles’ “longstanding commitment to community service, as 
evidenced by his successful tenure at SKYE” along with his “comprehensive 
understanding of broadcast operations, combined with a practical approach to education 
and community engagement.” Id. GCWW opines that this makes Mr. Coles “an 
outstanding choice to helm these operations” and that Mr. Coles “possesses the 
leadership qualities necessary to fully realize the studio's potential as a hub for community 
enrichment through education and hands-on learning.” Id. The treasurer of the GWCC, 
Terrence S. McAuliffe, also provided an individual recommendation, which is addressed 
in Section III.A.8, below. 
2. A review of the organization's or the company's performance in 
providing community access programming. 
As this is a new nonprofit, the Authority does not have the ability to review the 
organization’s performance in providing community access programing. However, as 
discussed in Section III.A.4 below, Mr. Coles and Ms. Fitzgerald both have significant 
experience in community access operations and production from their tenure at Skye. 
The Authority is confident that the individual experiences can be properly imputed onto 
Brass City. 
3. The operating plan submitted by the organization and the company for 
providing community access programming. 
Brass City will be run by Mr. Coles, serving as Executive Director. Petition, p. 1. 
Mr. Coles has close to 35 years of experience in community access television, with 26 of 
those being with Skye. Id. Joining Mr. Coles is Ms. Fitzpatrick as Program Director. 
Petition, p. 1. Ms. Fitzpatrick has 18 years’ experience working in public access, including 
8 years at Skye. Id. Brass City plans to continue operations out of the current Skye 
location with uninterrupted access and with minimal to no down time or blackout period. 
Id., p. 2. Brass City also anticipates extending the hours the studio is open (currently half 
days on the weekends), to provide additional community outreach, especially to more 
underserved groups and communities, and to develop a more collaborative relationship 
with the local school administrations with the goal of having students creating content 
once again to air over the Educational Access channel. Id., p. 4. 
4. The experience in community access programming of the organization. 
As this is a new nonprofit, the Authority does not have the ability to review the 
organization’s experience in community access. However, Mr. Coles and Ms. Fitzgerald 
both have significant experience in community access operations and production from 
their tenure at Skye. The Authority is confident that this experience can be properly 
imputed onto Brass City. 
5. The organization's and the company's proposed budget, including 
expenses for salaries, consultants, attorneys, and other professionals. 
Brass City provided an estimated budget of $255,000, $245,000, and $235,000 for 
the years 2024 through 2026 in support of its petition. Petition, Att. 2, p. 1. The projection 
is based on Skye’s 2021 annual report (Skye’s most recently filed report). Id. Salaries 
are anticipated to be Brass City’s biggest expense at $140,000 for 2024 increasing to 

Docket No. 24-01-41 
Page 4 

$150,000 for 2025. Following salaries, rent, legal/professional fees, insurance, and 
telephones/utilities make up the largest expenses with totals ranging from $10,000 for 
insurance to $35,400 for rent in 2024, as an example. Id. The proposed budget is in line 
with Skye’s budget from previous years and shows moderate increases, which are not 
out of line with inflation. The budget submitted is reasonable under the circumstances 
and based on the best information available. 
6. The quality and quantity of the programming to be created, promoted or 
facilitated by the organization or the company. 
While the Petition does not go into depth on the quantity of programing to be 
created by Brass City, it does discuss facilitating increased educational content and 
continuing to strengthen ties with the local government for government content. Petition, 
p. 3. Brass City intends to revitalize educational content by working collaboratively with 
the Waterbury Arts Magnet School. Petition, p. 3. Brass City also intends to continue the 
Skye operations without interruption, indicating that the programing currently being 
produced will continue. Id., p. 2. Brass City also intends to “provide additional community 
outreach, especially to more underserved groups and communities, to foster a more 
inclusive environment, and promote a more diverse program lineup that reflects the 
diversity of the communities we serve.” Id., p. 3. 
7. A review of the organization's procedures to ensure compliance with 
federal and state law, including the regulations of Connecticut state 
agencies. 
Brass City is familiar with and is committed to complying with all federal and state 
laws. Petition, p. 4. Brass City also intends to continue the relationship Skye has with 
Kim Fisher, a nonprofit strategist/consultant, and to retain legal counsel as part of Brass 
City’s yearly budget. Id. Brass City’s Policies and Procedures reference and discuss 
relevant PURA regulations and demonstrate that Brass City is prepared to comply with 
applicable regulations. Id., Att. 3. 
8. Any other criteria determined to be relevant by the authority. 
The Authority concludes that no additional criteria must be examined at this time. 
However, the Authority notes that additional comments were received from the public. 
The Authority received correspondence from Attorney F. David Corbett who 
wholeheartedly offered his support for Mr. Coles. Corbett Corresp., May 1, 2024. 
Attorney Corbett taught Mr. Coles in the 1970s and also worked with him when Attorney 
Corbett had a community access show on Skye Cable from 1996 to 2015. Id. Attorney 
Corbett states that Mr. Coles is “a great mentor, teacher and leader” and that he cannot 
identify a person “more qualified to lead a public access station than Alphonso Coles.” Id. 
As mentioned above, the treasurer of the GWCC, Terrence S. McAuliffe, who is 
also the owner of Tribury Media, LLC, provided an individual letter of recommendation in 
addition to the GWCC letter. Petition, Att. 4.2. Mr. McAuliffe spoke of Mr. Coles’ “technical 
proficiency, combined with his profound commitment to fostering a community-centric 
broadcasting environment” as well as his “eagerness to mentor and educate community 
members and staff alike in the intricacies of media production” and his commitment to 
empowerment through education. Id.

IV. 
CONCLUSION AND ORDERS 
A. 
CONCLUSION 
A review of the materials presented by Brass City and in support of Brass City 
demonstrates that Brass City is well equipped to assume community access provider 
duties as Skye winds down its operation. As a result, the Authority directs Brass City to 
assume the Community Access Provider designation as well as the responsibilities for 
and the control of operations at the access facility, which are currently designated to and 
controlled by Skye. The Authority further directs Skye to work with Brass City to effectuate 
a smooth transfer of operations and assets. 
B. 
ORDERS 
For orders requiring a filing, Brass City shall file an electronic version through the 
Authority’s website at www.ct.gov/pura. Submissions filed in compliance with the 
Authority’s orders must be identified by: Docket Number, Title, and Order Number. 
Compliance with orders shall commence and continue as indicated in each specific order 
or until Brass City requests and the Authority approves that Brass City’s compliance is no 
longer required after a certain date. Unless otherwise provided or determined by the 
Authority, filings submitted in compliance with an order shall constitute satisfaction of the 
order. Filings requiring Authority approval must be filed as a motion. 
1. 
Skye and Brass City are directed to work together to effectuate smooth transfer of 
both the community access operations and the assets identified by Skye. 
2. 
Upon the completion of the transfer, Brass City shall file compliance in this docket 
indicating that it has assumed Skye’s community access provider duties. 
3. 
Upon completion of the transfer, Brass City shall provide written confirmation to its 
area MVPDs to alert them to the transfer of duties and to ensure the smooth 
transfer of the MVPDs support obligations. 
4. 
Following the completion of the transfer, Brass City is directed to file an 
appearance in any active Authority docket in which Skye currently is a party, 
participant, or intervenor to alert all docket participant of the transfer. The 
appearance shall indicate that any communications or filings previously directed 
to Skye should thereafter be directed to Brass City. This includes but is not limited 
to the Annual Allocation of Public Educational and Governmental Programming 
and Education Technology Investment Account (Docket No. 23-10-02) the Annual 
Community Access Support docket (Docket No. 24-01-06).
